name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-fifteen-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 15 and receives exact float4 zero from all fourteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A seventeen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: border-colour-texels-of-r16float-r16uint-rgba16sint
rationale: clamp_to_border with each of Metal's three border colours per bound pixel format (the Metal-oracle border and alpha observations; The product maps ClampToBorderColor to Vulkan's CLAMP_TO_BORDER with the matching float or INT_* border colour, and leaves open what a format without alpha, or with fewer channels, returns at the border). This case binds r16_float to the float texture 0, r16_uint to the uint texture 1, and rgba16_sint to the int texture 2, each 4x4 with every texel equal: the float texture's channels hold 1.0 (0xFF for unorm), the uint texture's (1, 2, 3, 4) and the int texture's (-1, 2, -3, 4), truncated to the format's channels. Lane t reads a normalized coordinate from buffer 0 and writes ten uint4s of raw bits to buffer 1 through constexpr clamp_to_border samplers at explicit level 0: the float texture with nearest transparent_black, opaque_black and opaque_white borders and a linear opaque_white one (out[10t] .. out[10t+3]), then the uint (out[10t+4] .. out[10t+6]) and int (out[10t+7] .. out[10t+9]) textures with the three nearest samplers. The coordinates are (0.125, 0.125), (0.875, 0.625), (-0.125, 0.375), (1.125, 0.375), (0.375, -0.125), (0.375, 1.125), (-0.125, -0.125), (1.5, 1.5), (0, 0.375), (1, 0.375), (0.375, 0), (0.375, 1), (0, 0), (-0.0625, 0.375), (1.0625, 0.625), (0.625, 0.625): texel centres inside, points outside each side and corner, and points on each edge and a quarter texel outside, so nearest lanes outside read the border texel itself (a nearest sample at u = 1.0 selects texel 4, outside) and the linear lanes on an edge blend the in-range texel with the opaque-white border at weights 1/2, 1/4 and 3/4. All in-range values and weights are dyadic, so every expected value is exact. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB so an unwritten word is visible; each lane writes only its own ten uint4s; the AIR has no loop.

name: global-built-ins-in-a-24x5x2-grid-of-8x4-threadgroups
rationale: Metal 3.1's program-scope built-in variables: every kernel built-in declared as a global uint or uint3 and read in the kernel (the simdgroup and quad lanes in an out-of-line helper), each thread writing 29 words at out[29 t] (buffer 0, pre-filled with 0xAB), t its linear position in the grid. dispatchThreads of a 24x5x2 grid in 8x4x1 threadgroups: threadgroups_per_grid is (3, 2, 2), and the threadgroups of the last row hold one row of threads (threads_per_threadgroup (8, 1, 1), 8 threads, one simdgroup, two quads) while dispatch_threads_per_threadgroup stays (8, 4, 1) and dispatch_simdgroups_per_threadgroup 1; the full threadgroups are one simdgroup of 32 lanes and 8 quads. The AIR has no loop.

name: global-built-ins-in-a-7x3x3-grid-of-4x2x2-threadgroups
rationale: Metal 3.1's program-scope built-in variables, as in the 24x5x2 case: dispatchThreads of a 7x3x3 grid in 4x2x2 threadgroups, partial on every axis: threadgroups_per_grid is (2, 2, 2), and a threadgroup at the far edge of an axis holds 3 threads on x, 1 on y or 1 on z (its threads_per_threadgroup), while dispatch_threads_per_threadgroup stays (4, 2, 2). Buffer 0 pre-filled with 0xAB, 29 words per thread. The AIR has no loop.

name: global-built-ins-in-one-threadgroup-of-two-simdgroups
rationale: Metal 3.1's program-scope built-in variables, as in the 24x5x2 case: one threadgroup of 40 threads, two simdgroups (32 lanes, then 8) and ten quads; simdgroups_per_threadgroup and dispatch_simdgroups_per_threadgroup are 2, thread_index_in_simdgroup runs 0 to 31 then 0 to 7, and simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup is 0 then 1. Buffer 0 pre-filled with 0xAB, 29 words per thread. The AIR has no loop.

name: fragment-alpha-float-to-half4-white
rationale: The fragment truncates its scalar float alpha varying to half and returns half4 (1,1,1,alpha); the generated fullscreen vertex stage supplies alpha and the complete pixel captures the conversion.

name: clamp-a-negative-signed-origin-onto-the-first-int-array-column
rationale: The copy's `source_origin` is a `short3`, so this case gives it a negative x and lets the clamp report which conversion the sample coordinate went through. A 4x4x2 grid runs 32 threads; the guard is `destination_size.xy` = (3, 2), so the 12 threads with gid.x < 3 and gid.y < 2 survive -- gid.z is never bounded, so the two array layers are exactly the dispatch's z extent. A surviving thread samples src at the unnormalized coordinate float2(source_origin + gid).xy = (gid.x - 1, gid.y + 1) with array index uint(float(gid.z)), and writes the int4 to dest at (destination_origin + gid) = (1 + gid.x, 1 + gid.y, gid.z). The sampler is unnormalized nearest with no mip and clamp_to_edge, so the sample is an exact texel fetch and the only rounding is the address clamp. That clamp is the whole point: gid.x = 0 gives the coordinate -1.0, which clamp_to_edge pulls to column 0 -- the same column gid.x = 1 reads at coordinate 0.0 -- while gid.x = 2 reads column 1. So dest columns 1 and 2 must hold identical texels and column 3 must differ. Had the short3 been widened unsigned, -1 would have been 65535, whose clamp is column 3, and the duplicate pair would break. Source texels are the negative and positive of 4096 + layer*256 + y*16 + x in red and green, x - 3 in blue and 2*layer - 1 in alpha, so every copied texel names its own source coordinate, red carries a sign the format has to keep, and a layer or axis swap is visible in the bytes. The 20 texels outside the destination window keep their 0xCC poison, which is what shows the guard held.

name: vertex-float2-position-expansion
rationale: Three authored float2 positions form a full-coverage triangle; the typed observer captures their structural expansion to clip-space float4 (x,y,0,1).

name: vertex-float2-varying-passthrough
rationale: Three authored positions form a full-coverage triangle and constant float2 attributes traverse varying location zero into the typed observer.

name: linked-k48-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-bfloat-64-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry, whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 128 lanes (4 simdgroups) runs the single 64x64 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 64, K = 48 (one whole 32-deep block, the unsafe loader, and a 16-deep remainder, the safe one). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 32 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (expert strides w, scales and biases batch stride = N*K = 3072), writing only its own rows. W[e][n][k] (w_ld = 48 bytes): both experts hold q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (63 of the 64 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads); expert 0's scales repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and expert 1's are half of them (biases unread without the bias bit). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . W/2 = a . W): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (256 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Each dequantized weight is a multiple of 0.25 at most 30, exact in bfloat, and each x at most 10; each product with x a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-bfloat
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A one-thread zero-extent bfloat gather quantized-matrix-multiply invocation bounds every loop and retains the poisoned four-byte destination. The two direct visible references are supplied by prior-qualified modules with exact scalar and float4 callback ABI signatures. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: linked-single-unit-average-write
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, threadgroup cube, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. The required multi-destination constants declare one float source at table element zero and one active float destination at element one, so the small-parameter average path executes only its unit window and bounded single invocation before writing exact one.

name: a-mesh-function-marks-each-threadgroup-of-its-grid
rationale: icb_mesh_marks without rasterization under a grid of 2 threadgroups of 4 threads: each threadgroup's thread 0 writes its position, the grid's threadgroups and its threads, one byte per axis, and 0xd0000000 plus its index, into the word of its index in mesh buffer 0; the third word stays as the bytes 0xab. The template of the cases whose kernels encode mesh draws into an indirect command buffer.

name: an-object-function-reads-a-word-and-launches-no-mesh-threadgroup
rationale: icb_object_reader without rasterization, one object threadgroup of one thread under its partner icb_mesh_triangle: it reads word 0 of object buffer 0, (5, 6, 7, 8), writes it doubled plus one into word 1, and launches no mesh threadgroup, so its partner draws nothing. The reader template of the case whose kernel encodes a barrier between a writer's mesh draw and its own.

name: bit-manipulation-edge-words
rationale: Every LLVM bit-manipulation intrinsic Metal's compiler emits from MSL, in one loop-free kernel: llvm.bitreverse of i8, i16, i32, i64 and <4 x i32>; llvm.bswap of i16, i32, i64 and <4 x i32>; llvm.fshl and llvm.fshr as rotations of i8, i16, i32 and i64 and fshl of <4 x i32>; llvm.ctpop of i32 and i64; llvm.ctlz and llvm.cttz of i16 with the zero-poison flag, and of i32 and i64 with it both ways. Each of the 16 threads reads one 64-bit word and one amount and writes 43 words of its 48-word block; the other five keep the 0xab fill. The words are the edge values: zero, all ones, the top bit of each width alone (1 << 63, 0x80000000, 0x8000, 0x80), one, the low and high halves alone, alternating bits, irregular words, and 0x7f, 0x7fff and 1 << 32 at the width boundaries; the amounts are 0, 1, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 3, 100, 255 and 0xffffffff, so each rotation meets an amount of zero, of its width, and past it. A flag-false count reads zero (answered by the width); a flag-true count reads only non-zero operands.

name: bit-manipulation-mixed-words
rationale: The kernel of bit-manipulation-edge-words over 32 irregular 64-bit words (splitmix64 of multiples of 0x1234567) and 32 amounts from 2 to 0xfffffffe, so each rotation, byte swap, bit reversal and count meets dense words whose two 32-bit halves differ, with amounts in every residue of each width and past 2^16 and 2^31; the lanes of the <4 x i32> forms each hold another word.

name: vertex-attribute-fetches-past-its-vertex-buffer
rationale: Eight points over a four-element vertex buffer: vertices 4 to 7 fetch attribute 0 past it. Metal's fetch is unchecked, so the oracle binds the buffer with a 16-byte shadow past it and records zero for out[4..8]; the candidate's fetch is fixed-function under buffer robustness or pulled with its own check.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: write-every-face-of-a-cube-at-a-level-read-from-a-buffer
rationale: Ninety-six threads write (gid.x, gid.y, gid.z, 1) at texel gid.xy of face gid.z of a 4x4 rgba32_float storage cube at the level lod read from constant uint buffer 0 (texture.write through the cube slot's level views, each a 2D-array view of one level). lod = 0, the cube's only level, so every write is defined: texel (x, y) of face f becomes (x, y, f, 1); all six faces are compared, so a write that lost its face or level leaves the 0xab initial bytes. The AIR has no loop.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-five
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 5 and receives exact float4 zero from all four linked _uber_clear bodies. A seven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: linked-single-unit-ArrayMultiplyTNLinking
rationale: One invocation multiplies a 1x1 matrix pair with K equal to one. Matrix dimensions, batch counts, split counts, and NDArray extents are one; row and allocation byte strides are the exact four-byte float width, bounding every matrix and batch loop. The array declares three elements. Metal reports the third as `missing Buffer binding at index 2 for buffers.2[0]`, so every earlier observation of this case read undefined memory for it. It is authored 3.0, distinct from the 1.0 of element zero, and the written value was measured invariant under it: setting the operand pair to 2.0 and 3.0 also writes zero. This case pins the zero the linked kernel writes, not a product.

name: inverse-square-root-of-four-powers-of-four
rationale: W, H and C4*n_batch are all one, so the single invocation is the only one that passes the three bounds and its texel is the whole answer. eps is zero, so the value handed to the reciprocal square root is the source texel unchanged, and every lane is a power of four: 4, 1/4, 16 and 1 invert to 0.5, 2, 0.25 and 1, all exactly representable in binary32 and all fixed points of any Newton refinement, so the fast variant has nowhere to differ.

name: depthwise-conv3d-grad-backprop-2x2x1-three-channels-writes-every-channel
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-work case of this entry, whose zero sizes stop every thread. User constant 124 = 0x01000011: kernel 2x2x1 and unit strides from the constant (smallParamsFC 1), no channel multiplier, channel axis 0 (coordinate (c, x, y, z)), no gradient accumulation (the write goes to postfixPrimary_f); constant 112 = 0 (padding mode 0). The data gradient's size is (W, H, D, C) = (3, 2, 2, 3) and the gradient's the same, unit dilations, zero offsets, recipStrides 1. C = 3 is below the four-channel fast path, so each thread takes the per-channel loop: for c = 0, 1, 2 it sums the 2x2x1 taps whose stride test passes and, when its position is inside the data gradient, writes coordinate (c, x, y, z). One threadgroup of 4x2x2 threads: the 12 with x below 3 write, the 4 with x = 3 compute and write nothing. The coordinate's first component is c, so words 0 to 2 are written and words 3 to 5 keep the 0xab fill. The retained modules of the source callbacks the case links return constants (prefixSecondary_f and prefixTertiary_f 0.0; the only retained modules of those functions), so every product is 0.0 and every sum exactly +0.0 in any order; every writer of a word stores that same value, so the observed words do not depend on write order. The variant observes the loops, the bounds checks and the written coordinates through the linked writer (postfixPrimary_f, module aad641ec, table entry 1 at the coordinate's first component), not data-dependent arithmetic. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the channel loop runs C = 3 times and the tap loops the constant's kernel sizes 2, 2 and 1.

name: linked-zero-work-depthwise-convolution-3d-gradient-backprop
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The zeroed depthwise-gradient parameter record gives the one-invocation dispatch no output extent while the reference-size constant remains one. This provides finite loop bounds and observes the unchanged four-byte destination allocation. Each AIR direct callback is supplied by a prior-qualified exact-signature module. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twelve-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 12 and receives exact float4 zero from all eleven linked _uber_clear bodies. A fourteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x1 resource.

name: store-through-a-selected-base-and-test-a-nullable-pointer
rationale: Two shapes the translator cannot express with a pointer VALUE. A pointer that is null on half the lanes and is then tested against null, and a STORE through a base pointer selected between two different descriptors and then indexed -- emit_selected_pointer_store, 16 corpus sources and no authored case. That store cannot be a merged pointer in Logical SPIR-V, so the emitter replays it as a read-modify-write on BOTH arms, which is exactly the lowering this case pins: every lane writes into c AND into out, and only the selected one gets the new value. Lanes 0-3 write c[gid+8] = gid+8 and leave out[gid+8] holding what it already held; lanes 4-7 do the reverse. So out[8..11] must come back at its 0xAB initial pattern -- the read-modify-write has to preserve it bit for bit -- while out[12..15] gets 12, 13, 14, 15. The low lanes' writes are then observed by reading c back into out[16..19] = 8, 9, 10, 11, and the high lanes read c slots nobody wrote, giving out[20..23] = 0. The null test answers 0 on the lanes whose pointer is real and 1 on the lanes where the select chose null. Every value is an exact binary32 integer. An arm confusion in the store puts the marker in out[8..11] or leaves out[12..15] at 0xAB; a read-modify-write that writes a constant instead of the old value destroys out[8..11]; an inverted null test answers 1 on the first four lanes.

name: clip-away-every-vertex-of-a-triangle-with-a-negative-clip-distance
no_effect: Every vertex has a negative clip distance, so the primitive is clipped away and the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: The discriminating half of the clip-distance pair. Its sibling rotate-a-normal-in-a-vertex-stage-that-also-writes-a-clip-distance is byte-identical except for two bytes -- the half zNearReceiver at offset 64 of prepassParameterArray -- and proves only that a module carrying a ClipDistance builtin loads and runs. It cannot prove the distance is HONOURED, because its distance is positive and nothing is clipped either way. Here zNearReceiver is +2 against a clip-space z of 0.5, so clipDistance is -1.5 at all three vertices and the whole primitive lies outside the user clip half-space. A backend that honours the distance discards it and the render target keeps its 0xab initial bytes; a backend that ignores it rasterises the same full-coverage triangle its sibling does and writes (1, 2, 4, 1). The two possible answers are as far apart as a float4 can be, and the sibling establishes that this geometry DOES cover the pixel, so an empty target here cannot be blamed on the draw doing nothing.

name: rotate-a-normal-in-a-vertex-stage-that-also-writes-a-clip-distance
rationale: The first authored case on a module that emits a ClipDistance builtin. 85 of the 14579 corpus sources emit one and no case reached any of them: all 9 hosts that declare air.clip_distance and carry a case are FALLBACK, so stage_output's clip_distance_output_type and array_ty had never run under an authored case. vsViewportInstancing writes five stage outputs -- position, viewport_array_index, clip_distance, render_target_array_index and two float3 varyings -- which is also the widest stage-output tail any authored vertex case has. The observation is varying 0, normal = normalToCrWorld * normal_in, and every other input is chosen so nothing else can move it. normalToCrWorld is diag(2, 4, 8) with 16-byte columns at offsets 64, 80 and 96 of instanceConstants, and all three vertices carry the same normal (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), so the interpolated value is (1, 2, 4) at every covered pixel and the answer does not depend on where in the triangle the 1x1 target samples. The three lanes are distinct and each is exact in binary32, so a transposed matrix, a wrong column stride, or a dropped column all change the bytes. The clip distance has to be positive or there is nothing to observe: objectToCrWorld, viewMatrix and crwsReferencePosition are identity and zero, so the clip-space position is the authored vertex, z = 0.5, and zNearReceiver is the half -1, giving clipDistance = 1.5 at all three vertices. The positions (-1,-1), (3,-1), (-1,3) are the standard full-coverage triangle, so the single pixel is inside it. tileIndex is 7 and receiverPlaneDirection is (0.25, 0.5, 0.75), both written to outputs this case does not observe, so they exercise the rest of the stage-output tail without entering the expectation.

name: simd-variant-leftovers
rationale: Sixteen air.simd_* type variants the corpus reaches once each and that no authored case covered: air.simd_sum.v2f32, air.simd_sum.u.v2i32, air.simd_shuffle_xor.v4f32, air.simd_shuffle_xor.u.i16, air.simd_shuffle_xor.s.v2i16, air.simd_shuffle_up.v4f16, air.simd_shuffle_up.u.i8, air.simd_shuffle_up.u.i16, air.simd_shuffle_and_fill_down.v4f32, air.simd_shuffle_and_fill_down.v3f16, air.simd_prefix_inclusive_sum.f32, air.simd_prefix_exclusive_sum.u.i16, air.simd_min.s.v2i16, air.simd_max.s.v2i16, air.simd_broadcast_first.f32 and air.simd_all. One dispatch of 32 threads in one threadgroup is exactly one Apple simdgroup. Every reduction is over integers small enough to be exact in binary32 and in ushort at any association order, so a reassociating compiler cannot move a bit: the float pair sums to (528, 1056), the uint pair to (528, 1584), and the inclusive prefix at lane t is (t+1)(t+2)/2. That is deliberate -- what this case sees is a wrong LANE, not a wrong ULP, and the 32 lanes therefore carry 32 different values in every operand. simd_shuffle_up is undefined below its delta, so all three shuffle_up calls run unconditionally at top level and only the store is guarded; the half4 row uses an if/else and the two integer rows use a ternary on purpose, because the ternary is the OpSelect shape that SPIRV-Cross sinks a single-reader subgroup result into, so those rows exercise the materialization that stops it while the if/else rows show the same answers with no select in sight. Guarded lanes write 0xABCDABCD. simd_shuffle_and_fill_down needs no guard: stepping off the end into the filling vector is what the family is for. Results are bit-cast into one uint buffer, floats whole and halves and ushorts zero-extended, so a single output region carries every width without a conversion that would round.

name: store-three-widths-through-a-dynamic-byte-offset-particle-view
rationale:
The device evidence for `passes/access/dynamic_reinterpret.rs`, which was the coverage queue's head at 33 of 53 reached functions unverified. Its rules run 2,131 times over the cased corpus and never MATCH: `emit_dynamic_lane_address`, `emit_block_element_pointer`, `store_object`, `int_type_width`, `is_unsigned_int_width`, `vector_components` and `only_alignment_hint` had never executed under any authored case. An eprintln on each of them, swept over all 14,579 sources, found 37 modules that reach them and NOT ONE of them cased; this is the smallest, at 483 lines. Measured with covgain against every cased source and public fixture: 19 functions no cased source reaches, 17 of them in that file.

The shape the rule is named for: a `device uchar *` whose fields live at byte offsets read at RUNTIME out of a 264-byte constant header of 33 `{int offset, short type, short}` descriptors, each field then reinterpreted as a wider element and indexed by the thread id. Every offset here is authored, so the case decides the layout: the particle count at 0, `age` (float) at 16, `particle_id` (int) at 32, `user_data1` (float4) at 64, the color output (float4) at 128 and the size output at 192. That is four distinct reinterpret widths off one byte pointer -- 32-bit int, 32-bit float, 128-bit vector -- plus the two stores.

Descriptor 7 carries a type tag as well as an offset, and with `has_size3D/2D/1D` all false the helper switches on it: 5 stores a float3, 4 a float2, 3 a float. The tag is 5, so the widest arm runs and the store is a 12-byte write inside a 16-byte stride -- the four bytes it must NOT touch are the fill, and the comparison covers them. The other function constants are true so the unguarded header reads are the live ones; `has_color` true is what makes the float4 store fire.

The texture is constant (every texel 2.0 in red), so no filter or address mode can move the answer and the sample still runs; the age values 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 stay inside [0,1) so no border rule applies either. The scale chain is `texel.x * (user_data1 * 0.6f) * clamp(0.5)`: 2.0 and 0.5 are exact powers of two, so it is association-proof under fast math and the color is exactly `user_data1 * 0.6f`. `user_data1[p] = (p+1, p+2, p+3, p+4)` makes every one of the 16 written floats distinct, so a lane swap, a stride error or a wrong reinterpret width all move a value that nothing else could have produced.

The whole 256-byte buffer is compared while only 128 of its bytes are written, over an input that is 0xAB everywhere it is not an authored field, so a store that walks off its own region shows up as a lost fill.

name: loads-and-stores-past-a-thread-local-array
rationale: Eight threads (the sized array form). Each thread's Frame holds before[4], array[4], and after[8] (initialized to 0xB000000k, 0xA000000k, 0xD000000k), the entry's one thread-local object, so an index from -4 to 11 into array stays inside the frame. idx = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 11, -1, -4 (loads), then 2, 3, 4, 11, -1, -4, 7, 0 (stores), as signed ints. Thread t stores 0xC0000000 | t to array[idx[8 + t]] and then loads array[idx[t]]; its eight output words (out bytes 32t to 32t + 31) are the load, array's four words after the store, the bits the store changed before the array, those it changed past it, and 0xF0000000 | t. Threads 0, 1, and 7 store inside the array, threads 2 to 6 past it (their changed-bits word on the side the index reaches, which Metal leaves undefined, is a declared read); threads 4 to 7 load past it (their load word is a declared read). Every other word compares with Metal: the array's words show the stores past it changed nothing in it.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-six-rgb-lane-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 26 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-five linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-eight-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry splats the selected R, G, and B lanes into the complete poisoned 3x1 primary footprint byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-fourteen-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 14 and receives exact float4 zero from all thirteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A sixteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-qvm-t-half
rationale: A single invocation and unit gather batch select literal index zero from the authored buffers. The quantized K extent and vector-row count are zero while the quantization group size is one, making every accumulation and final postfix loop zero-trip and leaving the sole bounded destination element unchanged. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: an-object-function-s-threadgroup-memory-takes-the-encoder-s-lengths
rationale: mesh_object_memory_sums under one object threadgroup of 16 threads, its threadgroup(0) and threadgroup(1) arguments set to 64 and 256 bytes beside its static 16-word array, observed through its launch: each of its first 8 threads combines a word of each argument and of the array, written by other threads before the barrier, into its payload word, which the generated mesh function draws with the grid of one mesh threadgroup. A misplaced argument or array reads another's values.

name: initialize-atomic-depth-word
rationale: One loop-free invocation uses thread_position_in_grid.x zero as the sole aligned i32 index and unconditionally replaces the complete poisoned word with exact uint 0x40000000.

name: linked-single-radix9-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-9 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.
